scope: independent source-free causal topology transfer; not native integration
question: Can a bounded directed-energy local repair transfer a causal transition model to randomly relabeled state observations, including previously unseen action-dependent edges, using only two public anchor correspondences and sparse NEW intervention evidence, without losing OLD predictions?
hypothesis: Topology-informed point alignment plus local contradiction repair may outperform independent new-context tabular count controls under pure remap and sparse changed edges, but should not be presumed better than fully fitted Bayesian permutation+change mixtures and will likely fail an out-of-family random rewiring negative.

worlds.original_law: A secret directed Hamiltonian ring: action0 goes to successor, action1 predecessor; 0.88 target probability, otherwise uniform among the other 5.
worlds.two_contexts: OLD sensor labels are 0..5. NEW sensor labels are a random unobserved bijection permutation; every new source and destination is permuted. TWO anchors are supplied as public old->new sensor correspondences for distinct old sensors 0 and 3. Both model and controls receive these anchors.
worlds.changes: SENSOR_REMAP: graph exactly same under new labels. LOCAL_REWIRE: swap action1 destinations of two randomly chosen distinct old states before applying permutation. OUT_FAMILY: action1 new targets are drawn independently from six states with replacement and are not constrained to ring/row-swap family. Action0 remains old successor graph. Learners receive no family label, hidden edges, or permutation.
worlds.data: Each OLD row/action receives 6 independent observations (72 events). Each NEW row/action receives 2 observations (24 events). Held NEW has 96 independent outcomes per row/action (1,152/world). 12 seeds ×3 regimes=36 worlds, 41,472 held outcomes. OLD training readout frozen before NEW fit, retained after JSON serialization. No held labels in fitting.
worlds.source: Source-free deterministic FNV1a/xorshift32 streams keyed by experiment, seed, regime, phase, state, action; OLD/new data independently drawn. Permutations keyed separately. No overlap with ENERGY-DELAY-07, ENERGY-DEPENDENT-NULL-10 or any prior consumed seeds.

candidate: For each of the 24 candidate sensor bijections consistent with two anchors, score mapped OLD Dirichlet(.5) row predictions on NEW data, and choose maximum-likelihood bijection (no access to true map). Use that MAP alignment to transfer OLD row Dirichlet(.5) counts. Compute per-action/source local Bayesian reset-vs-stay evidence from mapped new observations and old mapped row counts, with prior reset .25, then use a hard contradiction gate when posterior reset>=.80; reset selected rows to NEW-only Dirichlet(.5), otherwise pool OLD+NEW counts. Preserve OLD frozen readout separately. This is a restricted, nontransformer directed-edge memory, not new learned topology discovery proof.
comparators: FULLY FITTED independent NEW-only per-(sensor,action) Dirichlet(.5) baseline
FULLY FITTED anchor-constrained Bayesian model averaging over all 24 permutations using mapped OLD Dirichlet(.5) row likelihoods and weighted pooled OLD+NEW predictions (no explicit NEW rewiring)

FULLY FITTED joint permutation-plus-action-edge-change Bayesian model: for each of 24 anchor-consistent mappings, each NEW action/state row likelihood is mixture of pooled OLD predictive and NEW-only Dirichlet(.5) predictive with reset prior .25; exact per-row integrated Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood; posterior over mappings and row resets marginalized in predictive. STRONGEST conventional comparator.
FULLY FITTED MAP sensor alignment with pooled OLD+NEW Dirichlet(.5) on every row (no repair), a matched conventional ablation
Privileged true permutation and old/new true target predictor, source-law oracle only, not a superiority target
fairness: All non-oracle learners see same 72 OLD, 24 NEW public transitions and two anchor correspondences, fixed 6x2 row count budget and no true family labels. Exact Bayesian baseline may maintain a posterior over 24 mappings; state computational advantage claims must be measured separately under matching source/inference cost. No source-family Bayes oracle is an expected-Brier superiority target.
metrics: held NEW multiclass Brier overall + per family and action
correct sensor permutation recovery (descriptive, never claim latent inference without anchors)
candidate false local reset in SENSOR_REMAP
NEW changed-edge target detection recall in LOCAL_REWIRE and OUT_FAMILY
OLD frozen prediction array exactly stable across NEW and JSON roundtrip (not independent process)
whole-experiment CPU and memory UNVERIFIED unless timed on common OS

frozen_decision.supported_dev_only: Candidate held NEW Brier improves >=.01 against strongest fully fitted non-privileged comparator across all 36 worlds AND <=1/12 SENSOR_REMAP worlds show any false reset AND OLD readout preserved 36/36 AND LOCAL_REWIRE mean Brier no worse than best fitted dynamic comparator+0.005. Independent native qualification still required.
frozen_decision.mixed_no_go: Candidate improves >=.01 over NEW-only Dirichlet on SENSOR_REMAP and LOCAL_REWIRE, but does not dominate best conventional mapping+change control or fails negative controls.
frozen_decision.negative_no_go: Valid experiment not meeting supported or mixed. Preserve negative out-of-family behavior.
frozen_decision.invalid: Bad sample quotas, pre/post train overlap, source readback mismatch, source-family knowledge leaked to candidate, true permutation given beyond anchors, prior seeds replayed, thresholds selected after score, omitted joint Bayesian strong comparator, or primary run before source commit.

custody: Prereg commit first; freeze and fetch exact executable before smoke/primary; primary frozen seeds once; store 36-world metrics and source in existing PR #1346; never repeat consumed seeds. No standalone canonical learner, owner checkpoint, runner, schedule or production change.
